settings.copy: Ember & Grain is an independent brewery and taproom on the riverfront — small-batch ales and lagers brewed with local grain, poured a few feet from the tanks that made them.

settings.eyebrow: What Ember & Grain is known for
settings.title: Small batches,
settings.intro: We didn't build the biggest brewery in the region — we built the one that cares most about every pint that leaves it. Here's what that means in practice.

features.title: Riverfront brewhouse & taproom
features.text: An oak, brick, and steel space on the Mill River with a glass wall onto the tanks — you watch the next batch while you drink the last one.

features.title: Local heritage grain
features.text: We malt barley grown within sixty miles, and we buy each season's harvest before it's planted. Fresher grain, truer flavor, and a reason to stay local.

features.title: Open fermentation
features.text: Our saisons and wild ales ferment in open vessels, letting the yeast and the riverside air do their work — a living process you can smell before you taste.

features.title: Barrel program
features.text: Old wine and spirits barrels from the region rest in our cellar for one to three years, turning simple stouts and sours into layered, ageable beers.

features.title: Seasonal small-batch runs
features.text: When a farm brings in something interesting — a new hop, an heirloom wheat — we brew it. Limited runs that vanish in a weekend and never come back the same.

features.title: The tasting room
features.text: A cozy room off the taproom for flights, cheese boards, and the stories behind each beer. It's where regulars and first-timers end up talking.

settings.title: Pouring
settings.intro: A snapshot of the current lineup. The list rotates as batches finish — if it's gone when you arrive, ask what's next in the tank.

items.name: Riverbend Pale Ale
items.description: Our flagship — bright citrus and pine from Cascade and Amarillo, a firm cracker malt body, and a dry, clean finish.

items.name: Grain & Ember Stout
items.description: Roasted barley, dark chocolate, and a whisper of smoked malt from our own kiln. Rich but surprisingly easy-drinking at 6.2%.

items.name: Mill River Saison
items.description: Open-fermented with a touch of our house wild yeast. Peppery, slightly funky, with a soft golden haze and a bone-dry ending.

items.name: Harvest Wheat
items.description: Brewed with this season's heirloom wheat and a little orange zest. A hazy, refreshing summer pour at 4.8%.

items.name: Cellar Door Barleywine
items.description: A year in bourbon barrels — toffee, vanilla, and dark fruit with a smooth, warming backbone. One to sip slowly.

settings.title: From homebrew kit to
settings.intro: A decade of grain, fire, and patience.

events.title: A stubborn homebrewer
events.text: Founder Marta Vale wins her third local homebrew competition with a saison made from her grandmother's grain plot. She starts planning something bigger.

events.title: The riverfront found
events.text: An abandoned wool mill on the Mill River — open brick, heavy timber, and enough room for a real brewhouse. Marta and two friends sign the lease.

events.title: First pint poured
events.text: After eighteen months of building and a brutal first winter, the taproom opens with three beers and a line around the block. The pale ale sells out by nightfall.

events.title: Barrel program begins
events.text: The cellar fills with regional wine and spirits barrels. Our first barleywine wins gold at the regional championships and sells out in a week.

events.title: The farm partnership
events.text: We formalize grain contracts with seven farms within sixty miles. Every beer brewed since carries a harvest year and a farm's name.

events.title: A decade on the river
events.text: Twenty-eight medals, a loyal taproom, and a rotating lineup that still surprises us. Here's to the next batch.

settings.title: Pour after
settings.intro: The taproom is full of regulars who'd rather argue about beer than about much else.

reviews.quote: I've been coming every Friday since they opened. The lineup changes so often there's always something new, and the staff actually know what they're talking about — not just pouring, but the story behind the tank.
reviews.author: Dana Whitfield

reviews.quote: Their saison is the reason I started homebrewing. I drove ninety minutes just to try the open-ferment release, and it was worth every mile. This is what craft beer should be.
reviews.author: Tom Osei

reviews.quote: We held our engagement party in the tasting room. They built a bespoke barrel-aged stout for the toasts. Our guests are still talking about it months later.
reviews.author: Renee & Sam

settings.title: Find us on the Mill River
settings.intro: Drop by for a flight, book a brewery tour, or ask about private events in the tasting room. We'd love to pour you something you haven't tried before.
